summary: Tested whether the trigger is the flag itself or the persisted commit index, and the construction-time run resolves it in favour of the latter: a single-voter cluster that had only run with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled carried a staged commit index of 0 (the observation records the value rather than assuming it), survived its first flagged restart with its configuration and leadership intact, then staged a commit index of 9 through its own writes while the flag was on, and lost the configuration entirely on the next flagged restart (zero servers, no leader). That explains how this escapes testing — a single restart right after enabling the feature looks harmless — and pins the trigger to the condition the finding already states: a configuration entry at or below the persisted commit index, with no covering snapshot. The harness records the staged value, configuration size and leadership at each phase, both comparisons are gated on the observed staged state rather than on the mode, and the interpretation records the refinement as pending that receipt with fresh execution requested.
